presentation.label: WAVE SHAPING
presentation.summary: Fold, saturation, tone, compression and width.
presentation.overview: A chain for adding weight, grit and control: wavefolding, saturation, tone, compression and stereo width. Tape, tube and inflator saturation give the drive stage three different characters.

controls.name: COMP

controls.name: MIX

controls.name: KLVL

presentation.overview: A single-head tape echo with wow, randomized flutter and tape age. Explore drifting repeats, worn tape texture and feedback, with free or beat-synced timing.

controls.doc: repeat bandwidth, flutter and noise; fresh at 0, worn at 127

presentation.label: SCENE MORPH
presentation.summary: Lock MIDI track parameters to scenes and morph them with the crossfader.
presentation.overview: MIDI Scenes brings scene locks to MIDI tracks. Hold a scene and edit MIDI parameters, then morph between scenes with the crossfader. Crossfader morphing with step parameter locks
Standalone MIDISC2.0: pre-trig scenes and pattern/Part sync

Move the crossfader to morph between the two sides. An empty side uses a trig lock when present, otherwise the underlying track value.

presentation.label: 20 CHANNELS
presentation.summary: Record eight stereo tracks, MAIN and CUE over USB at 44.1 kHz and 24 bits.
presentation.overview: This is octabam’s 20-channel USB output implementation. At high speed it sends each track after its effects and before its fader, plus the final MAIN and CUE buses. At full speed it sends the tracks’ stereo sum. Required USB MIDI support is included in the SDK source.
highlights: 20 channels at high speed: eight tracks plus MAIN and CUE
Recorded hardware evidence on both MKI and MKII
usage: Connect the Octatrack’s USB port to your recording host and choose its USB audio input. Use high-speed USB for all twenty channels.
Channels 1–16 are track 1–8 stereo pairs, 17–18 MAIN, and 19–20 CUE. Track channels are post-effects and pre-fader; MAIN/CUE include the mixdown.
Allow the stream to settle before recording: upstream reports reordered startup samples around 0.5–1.5 seconds after opening. Full-speed USB carries a stereo track sum.

limitations: USB output only. Host-to-Octatrack USB input variants are outside this import.
Requires the included internal USB MIDI dependency. Only one USB output layout can be composed.
Windows and Linux hosts have not been measured in this record.
A startup sample-reordering burst remains open. Master-on MAIN remains 32 samples behind track taps; toggling master can leave up to 32 stale CUE frames.

presentation.label: SCALE / ROOT
presentation.summary: Keep pitch edits and chromatic trig keys in one of 24 scales with a selectable root.
presentation.overview: Scale Quantizer adds SCALE, ROOT and GLIDE to PROJECT > CONTROL > SEQUENCER. Pitch turns and parameter locks move through scale degrees, and chromatic trig keys snap to the chosen scale. ROOT transposes the scale and keyboard. SCALE OFF restores stock pitch behavior.
highlights: Pitch knob, parameter locks and chromatic keys follow the scale
usage: Open PROJECT > CONTROL > SEQUENCER and set SCALE. OFF preserves stock pitch behavior; choose a scale to constrain notes.
Set ROOT to the key you want. Pitch edits step by scale degree; chromatic keys snap to a degree and key 1 plays the root.
SCALE, ROOT and GLIDE persist through project save/reload and battery RAM. Synth polyphony and synth glide features require SYNTH MACHINE, which is outside this import.

controls.name: GLIDE
controls.doc: OFF or 1–127 slide time; the track LEG setting controls legato. Synth features require the separate SYNTH MACHINE module.
